read_by: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table and derivation write-up
input: Hub-height 3-second gust (m/s), or 10 m gust with a height bridge, divided by the IEC class 50-year gust (Ve50 = 1.4 x Vref); tornado via an EF-scale gust proxy; no fixed range (extrapolation warns)
not_covered: SCADA and controls, electrical collection, substation and civil infrastructure (reviewed secondary units, no curve)
out_of_scope: Tropical-cyclone and hurricane wind (separate neighbouring cell)
missing_mechanisms: Operating, feathered and yaw state are flags only, with no numeric effect
next_version: Model v2.0 proposal (not indexed): separate straight-line and tornado direct-hit pathways with ordered damage states, narrowed to one turbine-equipment assembly on a 1,090 USD/kW (2023) denominator

how_to_use.share_of: Each part's default share of the physical replaceable base (blade 0.173, tower 0.169, nacelle 0.345, foundation 0.062, power electronics 0.037), times the exposed turbine fraction

outputs.scenario_dollars: conditional: needs an explicit value and exposure basis
outputs.yearly_loss: conditional: consumer-computed from sampled frequency and intensity, a coupling model and caps applied inside the simulation; curve spread not carried

conditions: IEC wind class selects the speed scale (default IEC II); a turbine design speed can override it
Hub height is required for 10 m input; the default 1/7 power-law exponent is flagged and a missing bridge fails closed
Tornado uses the same curves with a lower 50% point (D50 shift)
Default parts cover 0.749 of the physical base (blade 0.173 + tower 0.169 + nacelle 0.345 + foundation 0.062); power electronics 0.037 only when opted in

method.summary: Engineering-fit logistic curves on hub gust over the IEC 50-year gust, built from IEC design speeds, the NIST fragility method and EF4 case evidence; tornado is a curve shift

key_sources: IEC 61400-1 design classes and Ve50 = 1.4 x Vref (DTU_IEC_61400_1, ASHES_IEC_EXTREME_EVENTS)
NIST, Fragility curves, damage matrices and wind-induced loss estimation (NIST_FRAGILITY_METHOD)
US DOE, How do wind turbines survive severe weather and storms (DOE_SEVERE_WEATHER)
NASA Earth Observatory, Greenfield EF4 tornado damage (NASA_GREENFIELD_TORNADO)
judgment: The 50% damage points (D50 ratios) for every part are engineering fits
Curve steepness (k) for every part is an engineering fit for sparse evidence
Tornado direct-hit shifts of the 50% point (-0.05 to -0.12) are placeholders
Power electronics maximum damage of 0.3 is a judgment cap

checks.name: Financial range check (Hazard repo): value-envelope ceiling for wind-farm convective wind (shared lineage; no open industry loss figures found)

open_items: Blade, tower, nacelle and foundation damage are summed; a damage-state dependency matrix is still needed
Candidate v1.1 items not adopted: numeric yaw-error conditioner, tornado shift refinement, IEC class II/III offsets
